messages:
alex: quick heads-up — seeing a ~28% tokens/sec drop in perf benchmarks after merge 9f7ac3e. CI perf job /bench/inference/token_throughput failing. KV cache hit rate looks lower in prod traces.
ci-bot: CI perf job failed: token_throughput decreased from 12.8k t/s to 9.2k t/s (benchmark suite a72). https://ci/reports/2033
maria: :eyes: can you paste the flamegraph/profile? also which kernel variant was selected?
alex: uploading quick profile dump from staging (attached). Key notes: queueing_delay spiked, avg batch size dropped from 6.4 -> 2.1, KV hit 87% -> 53%.
ken: my hunch — the kernel selection fallback logic got reordered in the merge. If kernel picks a fallback path that disables prefix-KV caching fastpath we lose hits.
paul: which commit? 9f7ac3e was the scheduling refactor. I can bisect if you want.
alex: please hold the rollout for the PR. Starting bisect now. If anyone can repro locally run: `TEST_SCALE=50 ./scripts/run_bench --suite token_throughput --seed 42`
maria: quick profile snippet shows hot in `scheduler::enqueue_wait` and `kv_cache::lookup_and_miss` — looks like increased miss handling.
```
# top symbols (sampling)
40% scheduler::enqueue_wait
25% kv_cache::lookup_and_miss
10% kernel::select_best_path
```
ken: will instrument selection logs. adding verbose flag to runtime: `--select-log=trace`
deploy-bot: Rollout paused for PR 4721 (auto) — reason: perf regression detected by CI
paul: if bisect narrows to the scheduling reorder I'll open a revert. keeping note: small-batch path interacts with kernel_hint.
alex: thanks all. update after bisect. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility :hammer:
